summary: The Guardian reported that Global Counsel, the lobbying company Mandelson co-founded and part-owns, works for Palantir, and that although he resigned as a director in May 2024 he continued to hold shares according to Companies House; campaigners asked the Cabinet Secretary to release information on his role in the February 2025 Palantir visit.

summary: The Guardian reported that Downing Street refused FOI requests for briefings before the Prime Minister's visit to Palantir in Washington, saying in October 2025 there were no briefings or minutes 'as this was not a formal meeting'; a government spokesperson said 'Palantir is a longstanding investor in the UK'.
notes: Robert Booth, 5 Feb 2026. The article says requests about meetings between Palantir's leadership and Starmer and Boris Johnson were refused.

who: Luke Pollard (Defence minister); James Cartlidge; Jon Trickett and others
summary: Answering an urgent question on MOD contracts with Palantir, the minister said the new enterprise agreement was a direct award justified under the Procurement Act 2023, that the decision was the Defence Secretary's alone and that 'Peter Mandelson had no influence on the decision to award this contract'. Jon Trickett MP said he was aware that 'at least five or six senior civil servants in the Ministry of Defence have gone to work with Palantir'.
notes: Web page: https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2026-02-10/debates/FECED111-4FA8-4343-BFAF-18D6C13808D0/MinistryOfDefencePalantirContracts. Pollard replied that departing staff have obligations and that Palantir 'employs an awful lot of UK veterans'. Dr Ellie Chowns referred to a Times report of a Palantir party for MOD officials the next day.

summary: Ministry of Defence transparency return (MOD: senior officials' business meetings January to March 2026) lists Andrew Martin: a meeting with 'Palantir'; purpose given: 'Reception with discussion on business opportunities and priorities', on 2026-02-11.

who: Lord Coaker (Defence minister); Baroness Goldie; Lord Bellingham
summary: In the Lords the defence minister said no minutes were taken of the Prime Minister's visit to Palantir with the then ambassador, which he described as 'a routine visit', and that the decision to award the contract was made by the Defence Secretary alone.

organisation: Department of Health and Social Care
summary: The Guardian reported that a DHSC briefing for Wes Streeting before his June 2025 meeting with Louis Mosley said public perception of the Federated Data Platform 'has been affected by the profile of Palantir', and that WhatsApp messages Streeting published with Mandelson did not mention Palantir.

The MOD said the Palantir Enterprise Agreement was direct-awarded under Section 41 and Schedule 5 (paragraphs 6 and 7) of the Procurement Act 2023, that no ministers or former officials with prior links to Palantir were involved at any stage, and that the award decision was the Defence Secretary's.

The MOD said the Strategic Partnership Arrangement announced on 18 September 2025 was 'a nonbinding statement of intent' that created no financial commitments, and that the contract signed on 30 December 2025 followed full commercial and governance processes.

who: Clive Lewis MP; DHSC, Home Office, DSIT and MOD
organisation: Department of Health and Social Care
summary: DHSC said neither the Health Secretary nor any members of the department had met or corresponded with Lord Mandelson on Palantir; the Home Office said 'No such meetings took place'; DSIT gave a general answer on supplier due diligence; the MOD referred to the Humble Address process.
The MOD said: 'As the Secretary of State has publicly said, Peter Mandelson had no influence or involvement in the Defence Enterprise Agreement with Palantir.'

who: Baroness Anderson of Stoke-on-Trent (Cabinet Office minister); Baroness Finn
summary: Asked why the Palantir visit was not in the Prime Minister's transparency return, Cabinet Office ministers said 'it was not a meeting, and so minutes were not taken'.
notes: PQ HL14055. Web page: https://questions-statements.parliament.uk/written-questions/detail/2026-01-28/HL14055. Follows PQ 102820, which asked why the visit was out of scope of the PM's January-March 2025 return.

summary: The MOD said the Office of the UK Defence Attaché 'holds no record of the meeting as no formal record of the meeting was produced'.

who: Chris Ward (Cabinet Office minister); Martin Wrigley MP
summary: The Cabinet Office said Palantir is not a strategic supplier to government, with no plans to classify it as one, and that the two largest UK public sector contracts with Palantir, the NHS Federated Data Platform and the MOD Enterprise Agreement, were initially awarded by the previous government.

organisation: Department of Health and Social Care
summary: A Lords question cited reports that the Joint Chair of the North West London Acute Provider Collaborative had advised Palantir while advocating integration of patient-level data into its platform; the minister's answer set out NHS conflict-of-interest guidance.

Cabinet Office transparency return (Cabinet Office Senior Officials' Meetings, January to March 2026) lists Andrew Forzani: a meeting with 'Palantir'; purpose given: 'Andrew met the UK leadership of this supplier as part of a cadence of regular touchpoints throughout the year / They discussed the supplier's relationship w HMG and the supplier's ambitions in the UK market', on 2026-03-19.

The MOD said its relationship with Palantir had developed over the last decade and that the first formal Enterprise Agreement was signed in November 2022 under the previous government, following earlier operational use of Palantir software.

The Cabinet Office said it wrote to two MPs about the Palantir contract on 25 February 2026, noting that the Member for Brentwood and Ongar 'personally signed off the original spending approval for the contract during his time at the Cabinet Office under the previous Conservative government'.
The MOD said that, based on the information it holds, it is not aware of any communications sent by Lord Mandelson in relation to the contract with Palantir.

The Nerve reported that Palantir had recruited 32 UK government and public sector officials and an additional 37 current mid-ranking staff from the military, the NHS and government departments, and that four members of the House of Lords had advised Palantir.
notes: 24 April 2026 (Charlie Young, Ian Tucker, Carole Cadwalladr). The article does not set out its method; individual names it gives are not reproduced here unless confirmed by an official record or other reputable press.

summary: The MOD said Global Counsel staff were not present at the Prime Minister's visit to Palantir on 27 February 2025 and that the UK Defence Attaché had not corresponded or met with Global Counsel representatives since July 2024.

Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office transparency return (FCDO senior officials' business expenses, April to June 2026) lists Andy Bamford: travel claimed with the stated purpose 'Breakfast with Laurence Lee (Company: Palantir)', on 2026-04-30.
notes: Publication: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/fcdo-senior-officials-business-expenses-hospitality-and-meetings-april-to-june-2026 Laurence Lee took up his Palantir role in February 2024; ACOBA's conditions ran for two years from his last day in Crown service.

summary: Jon Trickett asked what meetings the Prime Minister has had with Palantir since May 2024; no answer is recorded in Parliament's written questions service as at 20 October 2026 (answer due 30 April 2026).
Closing a King's Speech debate, a government minister said: 'We are reviewing the federated data platform contract in advance of the break point.'

who: Darren Jones (Chief Secretary to the Prime Minister)
summary: Presenting the second tranche of Humble Address documents, the minister said references to Palantir and Anduril had not been redacted outside the Intelligence and Security Committee process, and said he challenged 'the assumption that the Government are developing a "close relationship" with Palantir'.
notes: Web page: https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2026-06-01/debates/D3A5D4C6-EC00-460C-A981-39C17B72A73C/LordMandelsonHumbleAddressGovernmentResponse. The volumes' methodology statement (para 38) says there 'has been particular public interest in information involving Global Counsel and Palantir': https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/6a213331a0006190a6f098c5/E03595100_HA_Volume_II_Part_I_Web.pdf

summary: The committee's report 'Rewiring the state: Delivering digital government' (HC 61) concluded that 'Palantir should not have such a significant role in the UK public sector', recommended exercising the February 2027 break clause in the Federated Data Platform contract, and asked the government to explain the £240 million direct award to Palantir.
notes: First Report of Session 2026-27, paragraphs 92-98. Publication record: https://committees-api.parliament.uk/api/Publications/53352

who: Sarah Jones (Home Office minister); Martin Wrigley MP
summary: The minister said Palantir was the preferred supplier for the National Firearms Licensing Management System after an open and competitive process run by the Police Digital Service and BlueLight Commercial, and that 'Palantir is not buying the job'.
notes: Web page: https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2026-06-08/debates/110C9C82-8170-4BCC-9294-B070D2482E30/PoliceAITrials. Mr Wrigley said Palantir's £7.5 million bid was 44% of the estimated £17 million value.

organisation: Department of Health and Social Care
summary: DHSC said three Palantir contractors have administrative permissions in NHS England's National Data Integration Tenant, and that 19 of 22 non-NHS England contractors doing data engineering are employed by Palantir or its supplier consortium.

who: Preet Kaur Gill (DHSC minister); Lee Dillon MP
organisation: Department of Health and Social Care
summary: DHSC said ministers were not informed of routine access arrangements in the National Data Integration Tenant of the Federated Data Platform before May 2026.

who: Stephen Doughty (FCDO minister); Mike Wood and Charlie Dewhirst MPs
summary: The FCDO said no correspondence or contact between the British Embassy and Global Counsel had been identified in relation to the Prime Minister's visit to Palantir.

who: Lord Coaker (Defence minister); Lord Gove; Baroness Chakrabarti
summary: In a Lords question on Palantir contracts, the defence minister said officials told him Palantir was 'the only available platform' for the MOD's needs; Lord Gove said that as a minister he saw how Palantir's technology 'helped to save lives in the NHS' and 'helped to ensure that those fleeing persecution from the Ukraine war could have a safe home in this country'.

who: Health and Social Care Committee (Commons); Preet Kaur Gill (minister)
summary: After a 16 June 2026 evidence session, the Health and Social Care Committee wrote to the minister recommending that Palantir's Federated Data Platform contract not be extended when it ends in March 2027, citing mistrust, contested evidence of benefits and alternative tools.
notes: Letter dated 8 July 2026, published 9 July 2026. The letter says the minister apologised at the committee for not telling the public Palantir had access to patient-identifiable data. Publication record: https://committees-api.parliament.uk/api/Publications/54095

summary: The MOD said the Palantir visit 'was organised by Ministry of Defence officials as part of the former Prime Minister's trip to Washington' and that defence officials invited the Defence Attaché; in November 2025 the FCDO had said 'Officials from our Embassy in Washington arranged this trip in the normal way'.

The MOD said it has no record of any meetings or correspondence involving Lord Mandelson in relation to the award of the Defence Enterprise Agreement with Palantir, and no formal correspondence with Global Counsel while he was ambassador.

who: Lord Watson of Wyre Forest (Tom Watson)
